evidence.paraphrase: Benji declares he has constructed a time machine.
evidence.quote: It should be obvious. I have built a time machine.

evidence.paraphrase: Benji clarifies the device is for traveling through time rather than measuring it.
evidence.quote: No, Bull. Not a machine for telling time; a machine for traveling through time or, actually, more or less around it.

evidence.paraphrase: Benji explains the machine works by arranging counteracting magnetic force fields to bend space and circumvent time.
evidence.quote: More or less, it is a matter of setting up the proper number of counteracting magnetic force fields, properly focused, in a proper relationship each with the other to bend the normal space factors in such a way as to circumvent time.

evidence.paraphrase: The distance of a time jump depends on available power; house current allows about a day per jump.
evidence.quote: The amount or period of time is a question of power. With only the regular house current I have connected now, about a day at a step is the limit.

evidence.paraphrase: A new special power line lets the machine jump five years at a time.
evidence.quote: With this added power, the machine can travel five years. Five years at a jump

evidence.paraphrase: Benji describes traveling backward in time from the coming morning to the previous afternoon.
evidence.quote: this coming morning at ten to seven, I took--and will take--the machine and I traveled back to ten to five yesterday afternoon

evidence.paraphrase: Benji claims to exist simultaneously in two places due to time travel.
evidence.quote: it is a fact that I am in two places at the same time--only on different circuits

evidence.paraphrase: One version of Benji operates the machine and vanishes, along with its doubled appearance.
evidence.quote: He fiddled with a dial or knob--and vanished. The double exposure look of the machine disappeared too.

evidence.paraphrase: Benji and Daisy disappear in the machine after twisting a knob.
evidence.quote: Benji twisted a knob and grinned. "Good-by now," he said. And they were gone.

evidence.paraphrase: Benji explains the machine appears doubled because it exists twice, creating extra force fields.
evidence.quote: But just now the machine is there twice. That creates further static force fields.

evidence.paraphrase: Benji plans to use his simultaneous presence as an alibi for crimes committed by his time-traveling double.
evidence.quote: So I couldn't possibly have driven your car up the steps and through the glass doors into the ancient history section of the museum.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator plans a trap timed to Benji's predicted reappearance from time travel.
evidence.quote: I am figuring on a little party; a little reception in honor of our first intrepid time traveler. A surprise party.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator removes all electric power so Benji's machine cannot escape when it reappears.
evidence.quote: I have had all electric power lines removed from that entire section of the house. There is no power. None.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator predicts Benji will be trapped because his machine will have no power to leave.
evidence.quote: Benji will work his dials and controls, frantically. Nothing will happen. No power.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator gradually accepts Benji's claim after seeing evidence of the doubled Benji.
evidence.quote: His story was unbelievable. But I was beginning to believe it--partly because of the machine there and the fact that I had seen two of him practically at once the evening before

evidence.paraphrase: Daisy realizes with astonishment that the time travel was real.
evidence.quote: "Benji, it was _true_ then! All that you were telling me about going through time was true!

evidence.paraphrase: Benji works as a physicist experimenting in his laboratory.
evidence.quote: He plodded ahead in the University Physics Department and fiddled around his lab whenever he could escape into it.

evidence.paraphrase: After touching the machine, the narrator experiences a vision of outer space and a spiral nebula.
evidence.quote: there I was resting comfortably on a small cloud in far outer space, watching a great spiral nebula whirling in infinite majesty through the vast, empty blackness
